summary: Astronaut Health Monitor is a desktop app for long-duration missions that turns daily self-checks into clear, personal health guidance. An astronaut logs 11 indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂, temperature, glucose, sleep, mood, body mass, water intake, exercise and symptoms. Each value is compared not with a textbook norm but with the astronaut's own baseline from their medical card, adjusted for chronic conditions and for the hazards active in the mission environment, based on NASA's 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight. The result is a green/yellow/red level, a concrete recommendation, and an interactive 3D body model that highlights the affected organs. A flight surgeon on Earth sees the whole crew, reviews every record and sends conclusions back to the spacecraft, taking the communication delay into account. On the Moon or Mars, Earth is minutes away, so crews must notice problems early and act on their own. Our tool gives them that early warning and keeps the doctor in the loop.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
Astronauts enter daily measurements and symptoms. The backend evaluates every record and stores recommendations; the 3D body model (organs, vessels, bones, muscles) is coloured by status, and clicking a body part explains what is wrong there and why. Astronauts see their history, mark recommended tasks as done and read the doctor's conclusions. The flight surgeon sees the entire crew of their mission and sends reports to the spacecraft.

HOW IT WORKS
Rules are stored in editable JSON files: indicators.json (thresholds as % or absolute deviation from the personal baseline, plus hard safety limits), conditions.json (8 chronic conditions that make thresholds stricter, e.g. mild asthma lowers the acceptable SpO₂ drop), hazards.json (6 hazards linked to indicators and body zones, active only in matching environments: LEO, lunar orbit/surface, Mars transit/surface, analog) and body_zones.json. Levels: green, yellow, red, gray (no data). Data lives in a local SQLite database, so the app works without a connection to Earth.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT
Personal baselines catch changes a population norm would miss (e.g. a person whose normal pulse is 60). Early, plain-language advice supports crew autonomy when communication with Earth is delayed, and the doctor gets a structured crew overview instead of raw numbers.

TOOLS
JavaScript, React 19, Vite, three.js with React Three Fiber and drei, Node.js, SQLite, Electron. Passwords are hashed with scrypt; every API method has a role-based access rule (an astronaut sees only their own data, a doctor sees their mission crew).

CREATIVITY AND FACTORS CONSIDERED
We combine three layers in one evaluation: the individual baseline, chronic conditions and the mission environment's hazards. The 3D model shows the result where it matters, on the body. We considered privacy between crew members, offline operation, communication delay, and only spaceflight-plausible conditions. Medical thresholds are simplified for the demo and are not clinical guidance.
